He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]]. ==Early life and high school career== Flemings was born in [[Newport News, Virginia]] and grew up in [[San Antonio|San Antonio, Texas]].{{Cite web |last=Roy |first=Matt |date=2024-05-26 |title=San Antonio AAU team fosters family bonds and D1 futures after a decade |url=https://news4sanantonio.com/newsletter-daily/san-antonio-aau-team-fosters-family-bonds-and-d1-futures-after-a-decade |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=WOAI |language=en}} He attended [[William J. Brennan High School]] in San Antonio.{{cite web |title=2025–26 Men's Basketball Roster |url=https://uhcougars.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kingston-flemings/9545 |publisher=University of Houston}} During his freshman year, Flemings averaged 14.7 points, 3.7 rebounds and 6.1 assists over forty games, propelling his team to the UIL 6A Regional Finals. He set a single-season program record with 245 assists, showing his "good vision and instincts as a passer," as noted by his coach.{{cite web |title=Kingston Flemings Stats |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/tx/san-antonio/brennan-bears/athletes/kingston-flemings/basketball/stats/?careerid=drjhkaqbov6dd |website=MaxPreps |access-date=22 January 2026}}{{cite web |title=2022 Boys BB 6A Reg. 3 & 4 |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/tournament/z3UyE-RUEeuAzqREozo6lw/yAVQaeRVEeuAzqREozo6lw/basketball-21-22/2022-uil-texas-boys-state-basketball-championships-2022-boys-bb-6a-reg-3-and-4.htm |website=MaxPreps |access-date=22 January 2026}}{{cite web |last=Hinojosa |first=David |title=Freshman sensations pushed each other from the start |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/high-school/article/Freshman-sensations-pushed-each-other-from-the-16913468.php |website=San Antonio Express News |access-date=2026-01-22|date=2022-02-12}} As a sophomore, Flemings averaged 15.0 points, 5.2 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game, leading his team to a UIL 6A Regional title and a state semifinal appearance.{{cite web |title=2023 UIL 6A State Championship |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/tournament/lhh7c5A1Ee2A0wqb9tl3hA/zzjhuZA2Ee2A0wqb9tl3hA/basketball-22-23/2023-uil-texas-boys-state-basketball-championships-2023-uil-6a-state-championship.htm |website=MaxPreps}} He followed this as a junior by guiding the Bears to a 31–5 record and the UIL 6A Regional Semifinals; during that campaign, he averaged 17.4 points, 7.1 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 2.0 steals. Flemings finished his high school career by returning his team to the UIL 6A State Semifinals as a senior. That year, he posted career-high averages of 20.4 points, 6.8 assists and 2.9 steals per game. He also surpassed his own single-season program record by recording 246 assists, ultimately finishing his tenure at Brennan with a school-record 873 career assists. For his performances, Flemings was named [[Texas Mr. Basketball]], won the Gatorade Texas Player of the Year, was selected for the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], and received Naismith All-America Third Team honors. ===Recruiting=== Flemings was a consensus four-star recruit and regarded to be the best player in Texas, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web |title=Kingston Flemings |url=https://247sports.com/player/kingston-flemings-46135817/ |publisher=247 Sports}}{{cite web |title=Kingston Flemings |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/256112 |publisher=ESPN}}{{cite web |title=Kingston Flemings |url=https://www.on3.com/rivals/kingston-flemings-178202/ |publisher=On3}} On November 14, 2024, Flemings committed to [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] and [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite web |title=Kingston Flemings Joins Men’s Basketball in Signing Period |url=https://uhcougars.com/news/2024/11/14/kingston-flemings-inks-financial-aid-agreement-with-houston-mens-basketball |publisher=University of Houston}} {{College athlete recruit start|year=2025}} {{College athlete recruit entry|recruit=Kingston Flemings|position=[[Point guard]]|hometown=[[San Antonio, TX]]|highschool=[[William J. practices.{{cite web |title=Houston’s top-ranked recruiting class dives headfirst into summer workouts |url=https://thedailycougar.com/2025/06/07/nations-top-ranked-recruiting-class-dives-headfirst-into-houstons-summer-workouts/ |publisher=The Daily [[2025–26 Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball team|Lehigh]].{{cite web |title=Sampson earns 800th win as No. 2 Houston beats Lehigh 75-57 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401824809 |publisher=ESPN}} On November 17, Flemings was awarded the [[2025–26 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season#Big 12 Players of the Week|Big 12 Conference Player of the Week]] and [[Big 12 Conference]] Newcomer of the Week after averaging twenty points, eight assists and five rebounds a game in games against [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] and [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball|Oakland]].{{cite web |title=Kingston Flemings Sweeps Big 12 Weekly Awards |url=https://uhcougars.com/news/2025/11/17/mens-basketball-kingston-flemings-sweeps-big-12-weekly-awards |publisher=University of Houston}} On January 24, 2026, Flemings scored a season-high 42 points along with six assists and two steals in a 90–86 loss against [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]], setting a new Cougars freshman scoring record.{{cite web |title=Houston basketball freshman Kingston Flemings drops 42 in loss to Texas Tech |url=https://clutchpoints.com/ncaa-basketball/houston-basketball-news-kingston-flemings-42-loss-texas-tech |website=ClutchPoints}} He declared for the [[2026 NBA draft]] after the season.{{cite news |last=Shapiro |first=Michael |title=Kelvin Sampson gives 'inside scoop' on Kingston Flemings' NBA Draft decision |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/college/article/kingston-flemings-nba-draft-houston-kelvin-sampson-22197656.php |access-date=April 14, 2026 |work=[[Houston Chronicle]] |date=April 9, 2026}} ==Professional career== On June 23, 2026, Flemings was selected with the eighth overall pick by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fox5atlanta.com/sports/nba-draft-atlanta-hawks-select-kingston-flemings-eighth-overall|title=NBA draft: Atlanta Hawks select Kingston Flemings eighth overall|website=fox5atlanta.com|date=June 23, 2026|access-date=July 11, 2026}} ==National team career== Flemings represented the [[United States men's national under-18 3x3 team|United States]] at the [[2024 FIBA 3x3 U18 World Cup – Men's tournament|2024 FIBA 3x3 Under-18 World Cup]] in Hungary. He helped his team win the gold medal in a 21–13 victory against [[Spain men's national under-18 basketball team|Spain]].
